text.role: Senior front-end engineer, accessibility and agentic development
text.tagline: I make accessible the web applications that companies around the world use every day, and I work with AI agents without shipping anything I have not verified.
text.mark2: 2025 · Accessibility as a product requirement, TestCafe
text.marksAlt: Technical milestones: Vite in 2024, accessibility as a product requirement and TestCafe in 2025, Playwright and the audit tool in 2026.
text.measureCaption: Sixteen years in the trade, three employers, one product since 2015.
text.scaleNote: The scale above is proportional to how long each period actually lasted.
text.intro: I have been building web interfaces for sixteen years, almost always in JavaScript. Since 2015 I have worked at Four J's Development Tools on a web client that companies around the world use every day. The work comes down to three questions: does it hold up under load, will it still be maintainable in five years, and can everyone actually use it, keyboard and screen reader included.
text.quote: The kind of work where you live with your own code for years, and where one bad technical call keeps costing you for just as long.
text.dykLead: In France, digital accessibility is a legal obligation, checked and enforced, and no longer for the public sector alone.
text.dl1: Arcom, the French digital regulator, audits public websites and apps, with fines of up to €50,000.
text.dl2: The European Accessibility Act reaches the private sector: e-commerce, banking, transport, telecoms.
text.dl3: RGAA 5, the French framework aligned with WCAG 2.2, is due; a decree is expected in 2027.
text.dl4: End of the transition for services already in place.
text.offerLead: Accessibility specialist and hands-on front-end engineer, I can help as a consultant: RGAA and WCAG audits, an action plan, fixes in the code and automated tests.
text.a11yBody: WCAG, ARIA, keyboard navigation, screen readers. I handle it in the code, but mostly before the code: audits, automated checks in the build pipeline, design reviews with the product team. It is the part of the job I go deepest on, and the one that changes the most for the people using the product.
text.a11yBody2: The useful work starts where the tooling stops: knowing what a screen reader actually announces, and being able to argue a lint rule down, specification in hand, when it flags a false positive.
text.a11yStandards: Standards I work with: WCAG 2.2 (level AA), WAI-ARIA and the ARIA Authoring Practices, EN 301 549, RGAA 4.1.2 (the French accessibility framework). Keeping track of: RGAA 5 (announced for late 2026) and WCAG 3 (W3C draft).
text.jsBody: Fourteen years writing JavaScript, and above all maintaining it. I started when browser compatibility was done by hand, Internet Explorer 6 included. I have watched enough frameworks come and go to know what stays: the platform itself. I pick up a tool when it solves a problem I actually have.
text.aiBody: I work with coding agents every day: several sessions in parallel, each on its own copy of the repository, fixing, testing or reviewing. I also write what keeps them in line: skills shared with the team (source-backed accessibility review, end to end tests, ticket writing), automatic guardrails, project rules.
text.aiBody2: The time it saves is real, provided you stay the judge. A defect is reproduced before it is fixed, a fix goes past several verifier agents, and nothing generated ships without a test that failed before and passes after.
text.c1Context: C#, WPF, Silverlight. Line of business applications delivered straight to the people who would use them.
text.c1Focus: First lesson that stuck: the interface decides whether a tool gets used, not the engine behind it.
text.c2Context: Three years of JavaScript web development in medical diagnostics, inside what was then a Johnson & Johnson subsidiary.
text.c2Focus: The move to front-end for good, in a field where a misread screen is not a small thing.
text.c3Context: Building and evolving a web client that companies worldwide use every day, inside an international product team, in English.
text.c3Focus: Front-end architecture, performance, accessibility. Eleven years on one codebase: I still run into decisions I made five years ago.
text.shift2: TypeScript brought into the code and the tests
text.shift3: End to end suite rebuilt, from Protractor to TestCafe, then Playwright
text.shift4: Accessibility moved from bug fixing to product requirement
text.eduBody: Engineering degree in computer science, Conservatoire National des Arts et Métiers, June 2012. ITII Alsace programme.
text.skillsIntro: What I actually use, sorted by what it is for rather than by keyword.
text.sk1Items: JavaScript, TypeScript, SCSS, browser APIs, web standards
text.sk2Items: WCAG 2.2 AA, WAI-ARIA, EN 301 549, RGAA 4.1.2, keyboard navigation, screen readers (NVDA), axe, audits and reviews
text.sk3Items: Vitest for unit tests, Playwright and TestCafe for end to end, code review, automated checks
text.sk4Items: Large scale front-end architecture, browser performance, cross-browser compatibility, Vite and build tooling
text.sk5Items: Claude Code, skills, hooks, MCP, multi-agent orchestration
text.auditBody: An automated audit suite, built with Playwright, that walks a site and reports its accessibility defects with no setup: around twenty analysis modules, close to sixty rules, and a clear line between what actually blocks someone and what needs a human look.
text.auditBody2: It came out of a field observation: generic tools raise a lot of false positives, and miss what really gets in the way.
text.web3Body: Co-founder of two NFT collections on Solana, The Outfit and Gatsby Club, plus launch support for other projects: candy machine, storefront, mint. As much a founder's experience as an engineer's, in a setting where everything had to hold on launch day. A closed chapter.
text.offscreenBody: Trail running and hiking, and a few backpacking treks a year with my family: you carry what you need and nothing more. Chess too, for the pleasure of moves whose consequences only show up much later.
text.contactBody: Based in Strasbourg, used to working with a team spread across several countries. If your subject is accessibility, front-end architecture, or a codebase that has to last, get in touch.
text.contactGithub: Most of my work is proprietary and does not show up on GitHub, where you will mainly find personal projects. The andreas-brey account holds the recent ones, Fulgurus the older ones.
text.foot1: © 2026 Andréas Brey. One static page, no trackers, no cookies, no third party requests. Hand written, keyboard tested.
text.foot2: Set in Atkinson Hyperlegible Next, designed for low vision, and DM Mono.
